data.title: Platform Algorithm Manipulated to Extend Reach
data.summary:
Engagement was manufactured in the patterns platform ranking systems reward — rapid early
interaction, reply chains, and incentivised sharing — pushing campaign content into feeds
far beyond the operation's own following.
data.description:
Algorithmic amplification is the multiplier that makes small operations consequential. A
few hundred coordinated accounts generating the right early signals can place content in
front of audiences numbering in the millions, none of whom follow any campaign asset.

The manufactured signals are usually visible as a sharp, implausibly early engagement
spike followed by organic spread. Separating the two phases matters: the organic portion
consists of real people who now hold the belief, and they will not be addressed by a
report about inauthentic accounts.

Engagement figures therefore overstate the operation's size and understate its reach.
Both should be reported, and the difference between them explained.
data.recommendation:
* Separate manufactured from organic amplification in the analysis, and address the
  organic audience as genuine.
* Report the early engagement pattern to the platform, which is the part its ranking
  integrity teams act on.
* Do not infer the operation's size from its reach; state both and explain the difference.
data.short_recommendation: Separate manufactured from organic spread; report the early signal pattern.
